what_it_does: Azure Secure Hardware Architecture describes how Microsoft builds security directly into cloud server processors to protect customer workloads in shared data centers. The problem is that cloud servers run many untrusted customers' code on the same hardware, creating risk of data theft or side-channel attacks (where one customer infers secrets from another's power consumption or memory timing). Azure's solution integrates cryptographic verification (proof that code came from a trusted source), isolated execution zones (walled-off secure areas in the CPU where sensitive data cannot be accessed by untrusted code), and hardware-enforced key management (encryption keys locked inside the processor itself, inaccessible even to privileged software). This represents an extension of existing security primitives (trusted execution environments) adapted specifically for multi-tenant cloud threat models.
